item.title: ICCC warns PMV operators
item.description: PMV owners and operators who overcharge passengers under the newly approved fares have been warned that they will face hefty fines. Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] Commissioner Roy Daggy issued the warning on NBC’s Let’s Talk About It program in Port Moresby today.
item.content:encoded:
PMV owners and operators who overcharge passengers under the newly approved fares have been warned that they will face hefty fines.

Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] Commissioner Roy Daggy issued the warning on NBC’s Let’s Talk About It program in Port Moresby today.

The new PMV fares took effect Monday morning, with passengers paying a fare of K2 for all urban routes, regardless of distance travelled, including short trips such as from Foodland bus stop to 4-Mile bus stop.

Daggy says the ICCC will work closely with relevant authorities to ensure PMV and taxi operators comply with the approved fares.

Daggy emphasised that operators who fail to comply and overcharge passengers will face hefty fines.

Meanwhile, the ICCC will work with relevant authorities to ensure PMVs and taxis comply with the approved fares.

item.title: ACP Dalla calls for accountability and better management
item.description: Accountability and management were the main focus of the Highlands Eastern End Police Command's third-quarter meeting in Mt Hagen last week. Assistant Commissioner of Police Clement Dalla says police commanders must take responsibility for their duties and ensure that issues raised during previous meetings are properly addressed.
item.content:encoded:
Accountability and management were the main focus of the Highlands Eastern End Police Command's third-quarter meeting in Mt Hagen last week.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Clement Dalla says police commanders must take responsibility for their duties and ensure that issues raised during previous meetings are properly addressed.

Speaking at the meeting held at Airport Motel, ACP Dalla said the quarterly gatherings were important for reviewing police operations, identifying challenges and finding ways to improve service delivery.

He said the meeting brought together Provincial Police Commanders and other senior officers responsible for policing in Western Highlands, Jiwaka and Simbu provinces.

“Our agenda is normally centred around issues that affect our operations, the challenges we face and what we can do to improve on them.

“Much of the discussion during this one day third quarter meet was around accountability and management because this is a high-level management meeting for the command and that whatever items, issues at the PPCs closure must be reported back to the command with accountability and prudent management,” ACP Dalla said.

Dalla said police commanders discussed several issues affecting their daily operations, including logistics, funding and manpower shortages.

He stressed these challenges were common across government departments, but police must continue finding ways to work around them to ensure people receive the security and protection they need.

The meeting also reviewed action points carried forward from the previous two quarterly meetings.

ACP Dalla added some of the issues raised earlier had yet to be addressed, prompting him to urge provincial commanders to explain the progress they had made.

“Some of the agenda items were carried forward from our previous two quarterly meetings. Most of them were action items that had not been acted on.

“I urged the PPCs to go through each of these items and tell us exactly what they have done so far to address the issues raised of which the three PPCs of Simbu, Jiwaka, and Western Highlands have put forward." Dalla said.

He also said the quarterly meetings were not only about discussing problems but also about ensuring that decisions made by the command led to action.

The meetings cover both operational performance and administrative requirements, with the aim of improving the overall management of police services across the three provinces.

The Highlands Eastern End Police Divisional Commander added that the command would continue using these meetings to assess its performance, address outstanding issues and improve the way police services are delivered.

For the Highlands Eastern End Command, stronger accountability and management remain important in overcoming operational challenges and ensuring police officers can effectively carry out their duties.

item.title: Eastern Highlands leaders pay tribute to late Daulo MP
item.description: Mourners dressed in black, with mud smeared on their faces, gathered at Goroka Airport on Friday evening to welcome the body of late Daulo Member of Parliament (MP) Ekime Gorosahu, as Eastern Highlands Province paid its final respects to one of its leaders. Obura-Wonenara MP and Minister for Agriculture John Boito, alongside Henganofi MP and senior statesman Robert Atiyafa, paid tribute to Gorosah
item.content:encoded:
Mourners dressed in black, with mud smeared on their faces, gathered at Goroka Airport on Friday evening to welcome the body of late Daulo Member of Parliament (MP) Ekime Gorosahu, as Eastern Highlands Province paid its final respects to one of its leaders.

Obura-Wonenara MP and Minister for Agriculture John Boito, alongside Henganofi MP and senior statesman Robert Atiyafa, paid tribute to Gorosahu’s dedication to his people.

During the funeral eulogy, Boito recalled a story shared by Gorosahu’s son about his father’s concern for the people of Daulo, even during illness.

“In 2019, while seriously ill, Gorosahu said, ‘If I die today, I will not worry about anything but my people in Daulo,’” Boito recounted.

He also highlighted Gorosahu’s commitment to his duties, saying he continued carrying work documents even while confined to a wheelchair.

“Even while confined to a wheelchair, he remained dedicated to his duties, continuing to carry his work documents and serve the people of Daulo,” Boito said.

Meanwhile, Atiyafa urged Eastern Highlands residents to respect and appreciate their leaders while they are alive, rather than wait until their passing to recognise their worth.

“Let us appreciate our leaders while they are alive instead of accusing them or speaking hurtful words against them,” Atiyafa said.

Other Provincial Executive Council members, including Governor Simon Sia, Okapa MP Sonoma Saki and local-level government presidents, also paid their tribute to Gorosahu.

The late Gorosahu’s casket was escorted to the Provincial Miruso House of Assembly, where it was formally handed over by the National Parliament to the Provincial Executive Council and then to Daulo District representatives.

The Daulo District Development Authority will hold a formal ceremony later this week to hand over the casket to Gorosahu’s immediate family.

item.title: Child dies in house fire
item.description: A child tragically lost his life in a house fire this morning at the Games Village Police Barracks in Port Moresby. NCD Chief Superintendent for the PNG Fire Services, Saina Luwai, confirmed that the blaze completely destroyed the home of a police officer.
item.content:encoded:
A child tragically lost his life in a house fire this morning at the Games Village Police Barracks in Port Moresby.

NCD Chief Superintendent for the PNG Fire Services, Saina Luwai, confirmed that the blaze completely destroyed the home of a police officer.

He explained that although the Waigani Fire Station responded within five minutes of receiving the call, the house was already engulfed in flames and beyond saving.

Superintendent Luwai noted that the current El Niño conditions have made it dangerously easy for fires to ignite and spread.

While one child managed to escape, the other was trapped inside and could not be rescued.

According to reports from neighbors, two small children were in the house when the fire broke out.

The Fire Service will investigate the cause of the fire.

item.title: WSPHA farewells board chairman
item.description: The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) has officially farewelled its Board Chairman, Irad Nati. Nati was appointed in October 2024 with other board members, making history as the first permanent board for the PHA since its establishment in 2013.
item.content:encoded:
The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) has officially farewelled its Board Chairman, Irad Nati.

Nati was appointed in October 2024 with other board members, making history as the first permanent board for the PHA since its establishment in 2013.

WSPHA Chief Executive Officer, Stanley Masi, commended Mr. Nati for his outstanding leadership, saying the Authority has seen major improvements in governance and infrastructure under his chairmanship.

In his farewell speech, Nati said he was proud of the progress made despite challenges.

“Our role was to provide leadership, strengthen governance and ensure our people get the best healthcare services they deserve. I am pleased we have made meaningful progress,” he said.

Nati acknowledged ongoing challenges in funding, staff shortage and infrastructure but said a solid foundation has been laid for the PHA to move forward.

He challenged the incoming chairman to build on these achievements to deliver better health services for the people of West Sepik.

item.title: Martial Arts return to Kavieng
item.description: Taekwondo and Karate athletes across New Ireland Province converged in Kavieng yesterday afternoon as the Sir Julius Chan Bismarck Mixed Martial Arts Cup makes its comeback with the completion of day-one of the three-day championships at the Catholic Conference Centre. The tournament has brought together twelve martial arts clubs from across the province, giving male and female competitors an oppo
item.content:encoded:
Taekwondo and Karate athletes across New Ireland Province converged in Kavieng yesterday afternoon as the Sir Julius Chan Bismarck Mixed Martial Arts Cup makes its comeback with the completion of day-one of the three-day championships at the Catholic Conference Centre.

The tournament has brought together twelve martial arts clubs from across the province, giving male and female competitors an opportunity to test their skills, demonstrate discipline and compete for honours in the two codes.

Tournament Director, Severious Neki, says the cup tournament returns after a 10-year hiatus, thanks to the support of Governor Byron Chan and the New Ireland Provincial Administration.

Neki says the tournament forms the basis of a talent identification program where the best will be picked to form a provincial team to take part in the Karate Nationals in Lae next month (November) and the Taekwondo Korean Ambassadors' Cup in Port Moresby.

"We are honoured to have chief instructors from PNG Karate Federation in the likes of Vice President Sensei Roy Stanley, Sensei Abel Mekere and team from Port Moresby along with fellow Taekwondo professionals here with us.

"Martial arts isn't just a sport of defence and combat. Martial arts resonate mental control, self-discipline, respect and humility - values we want to encourage among the youth of today," Neki said.

The championships began with the grading category for both codes before going into the Karate Kata tournament in a show of pattern and sequence.

New Ireland Governor Byron Chan took time to be part of the program - he himself a sensei with affiliation and representation for international martial arts organisations around the world. Governor Chan said taekwondo and karate are more than just martial arts.

"They are disciplines that build character, instill respect, promote self-control and develop confidence among our young people. These values are important to New Ireland’s development aspirations because our future depends not only on economic growth and infrastructure, but also on raising a generation of disciplined, responsible and healthy citizens who can contribute positively to their communities.

“The New Ireland Provincial Government supports the revival of the Sir Julius Chan Bismarck Mixed Martial Arts Cup because we recognise the role sport plays in youth development, community engagement and the preservation of positive values. By investing in coaching, strengthening local clubs and creating opportunities for our athletes to compete, we are helping our young people discover their potential and develop skills that will serve them both inside and outside the sporting arena," the Governor said.

He said the Chan-Kolivos Government's vision is to see Taekwondo and Karate grow across the province, with stronger clubs, qualified instructors and a clear pathway for local athletes to compete at national and international levels, including the Pacific Games.

He said, “This is consistent with our broader development aspirations for a stronger, healthier and more empowered New Ireland, where young people are given opportunities to participate, develop their talents and play a meaningful role in building the future of our province.”

Meanwhile, the three-day tournament will feature Karate kata - patterns, Karate kumite - fighting, Taekwondo poomsae - patterns, and finishing off Monday with Taekwondo kyrugi - fighting.

Tournament instructors and rising martial artists, Steven Tommy from New Ireland and Vespa John of Kairuku, had been with the clubs last week, preparing for the tournament, running drills and coaching sessions.

John commended the Governor's support of martial arts, and the time taken to be part of the martial arts community in reviving what once was an annual cup tournament in Kavieng.

item.title: Kundiawa-Gembogl ballot boxes verified and await funding for recount
item.description: The PNG Electoral Commission has confirmed it can now comply with the National Court order for a recount of the Kundiawa-Gembogl Open electorate in Simbu, following a successful verification of ballot boxes in Kundiawa today. The verification exercise was conducted at the Kundiawa Police Station in a transparent manner, witnessed by key stakeholders and members of the public.
item.content:encoded:
The PNG Electoral Commission has confirmed it can now comply with the National Court order for a recount of the Kundiawa-Gembogl Open electorate in Simbu, following a successful verification of ballot boxes in Kundiawa today.

The verification exercise was conducted at the Kundiawa Police Station in a transparent manner, witnessed by key stakeholders and members of the public.

PNG Electoral Commissioner Dr. Nicole Haley said the inspection was witnessed by legal counsels for both the applicant and the respondent, two witnesses nominated by each party, a delegate registrar from Goroka, the Kundiawa Police Station Commander, and police personnel from Kundiawa and Goroka.

She said the primary purpose of the exercise was to ascertain and identify the ballot boxes from the 2021-2022 National General Election.

"We have now confirmed the ballot boxes are intact, so the court order can be complied with," Dr. Haley said.

She stressed that transparency would be maintained throughout the recount process.

"According to the court order, the recount must be conducted in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province. The decision was made to diffuse political tensions in Kundiawa and ensure the recount proceeds peacefully," she said.

She said the container holding the ballot boxes will now be transported from Kundiawa to Goroka under police escort.

She said they are now work on logistics and costing and will seek funding to facilitate the transfer and conduct of the recount.

The court-ordered recount for Kundiawa-Gembogl follows a lengthy election petition challenging the 2022 National General Election result.

item.title: More than a hundred receive King’s Golden Jubilee Medal
item.description: More than a hundred recipients of the Kings Golden Jubilee Medal at the 2026 Central Province Investiture Ceremony received medals and Certificates by His Excellency Grand Chief Sir Bob Dadae, Governor General of Papua New Guinea on Friday. The Kings Golden Jubilee Medal is awarded to individuals for their outstanding and Distinguished service to Papua New Guinea and Central Province. The Ceremony
item.content:encoded:
More than a hundred recipients of the Kings Golden Jubilee Medal at the 2026 Central Province Investiture Ceremony received medals and Certificates by His Excellency Grand Chief Sir Bob Dadae, Governor General of Papua New Guinea on Friday.

The Kings Golden Jubilee Medal is awarded to individuals for their outstanding and Distinguished service to Papua New Guinea and Central Province. The Ceremony at Bautama in Central Province saw 108 recipients awarded with their medals and certificates by his excellency grand chief Sir Bob Dadae and witnessed by their families, friends and colleagues.

Bill Toraso, Official Secretary congratulated the 2026 recipients and thanked them for their service.

“There are three different medals which are presented by his excellency through the same process, the one you are about to receive now is the 50 th Independence Anniversary Kings Golden Jubilee Medal.

“Gold medals that the Governor General presents are blessed by Buckingham palace, and they all recognize the individual contributions by the men and women of our country to develop the country." Toraso said.

Two serving staff of the National Broadcasting Corporation were also part of the cohort; Ms. Rachal Boga Director Provincial Radio at Radio Central and Mr. Wari Ila from the National Newsroom also received their medals for their services to Central and towards nation building in Papua New Guinea.

Acting Provincial Administrator, Magini Raga acknowledged the presence of his excellency and the recipients and apologized for the absence of Madam Governor and the District Members of the Province who had to attend the Parliament sitting.

“Our Nation's Golden Jubilee in 2025 celebrated 50 years of Papua New Guinea's sovereignty, resilience and growth. To my fellow recipients, congratulations and may this recognition inspire to continue serving our people with pride and dedication. May God bless our awardees.” Raga said.
